newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: No rapprochement with Bhutto, says Murtaza's widow.
newsitem.headline: No rapprochement with Bhutto, says Murtaza's widow.

text.p: Ghinwa Bhutto, widow of the slain brother of Benazir Bhutto, on Thursday ruled out any reconciliation with Pakistan's ousted prime minister.

"Benazir Bhutto could really have done something while in government in arresting the real culprits of Murtaza Bhutto's murder. She could have sheltered me and my children," Ghinwa told reporters in the southern city of Hyderabad.
"She attacked me and did nothing. Now when she is out of power, I do not see anything to talk about and compromise."
The Lebanese-born Ghinwa last month accepted leadership of her husband's breakaway faction of the Pakistan People's Party and plans to fight general elections set for February 3.
Murtaza Bhutto was killed along with seven companions in a shootout with police in still unexplained circumstances in Karachi on September 20. Police say his bodyguards fired first.

Bhutto has accused President Farooq Leghari, who sacked her government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, of murdering her estranged brother. The president has dismissed the allegation as ludicrous.
Murtaza's supporters accuse Zardari of involvement in a conspiracy to kill their leader. He denies the charge.
